outcome: Read-only Claude children: a chained read-only git command is refused with no refusal reason visible, so evaluators cannot check freeze fingerprints
acceptance: A read-only Claude child's denied Bash request gets a message that names the rule it broke and the allowed form, for at least chaining, redirection, git repository retargeting (`-C` and friends) and a `cd` away from the cwd; tests cover each.
The denial message names the delegation kind correctly (it does not call an evaluator a reviewer); a test covers an evaluator child.
The acceptance-evaluator brief states the read-only command form (one git command per call, run in the workspace, no -C, no cd elsewhere); a test pins it.
The full five-stage gate passes on the reviewed tree, and the review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.

completion.summary:
Read-only Claude delegation children, reviewers and acceptance evaluators, now get refusals that name the rule broken and the allowed form, and that say "delegation" rather than "reviewer". The rules covered:
- Bash: chaining, redirection (including `2>&1`), substitution, background, a cd away from the workspace on a git line (in the checker's own order), git's -C, --git-dir, --work-tree and -c, git help, listing-only git remote and branch, and unlisted commands;
- PowerShell, file edits, the tracker, and other tools.

The explanation lives in src/claude_read_only_refusal.rs and never decides; the allow/deny decision is unchanged. A Claude evaluator's brief states the allowed command form. A Codex evaluator's brief is unchanged, since it runs in its own sandbox.
